s1.syndrome_frame: a gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion
salient_findings: 2-year history of a mildly pruritic, erythematous, and gradually enlarging lesion
ill-defined, nonindurated, erythematous-violaceous plaque with an atrophic appearance
no improvement with topical corticosteroids and antifungals
key_facts: male patient in his early 70s
lesion located on the proximal portion of the left calf
lesion appeared without an identifiable cause
physical examination revealed an ill-defined, nonindurated, erythematous-violaceous plaque
lesion is slightly raised but with an atrophic appearance
histopathology showed band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis
no grenz zone found in histopathology
vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD34 and CD31
vascular channel endothelial cells were negative for D2-40
no hemosiderin deposits found with Perls Prussian blue stain

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches the clinical presentation of a pruritic, erythematous skin lesion with vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: angioma
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the histopathological findings of band-like vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: bacillary angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD34 and CD31

shortlist.label: pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: possible given the clinical presentation of a rapidly enlarging, erythematous lesion

shortlist.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the histopathological findings of round vascular channels lined by a single layer of endothelial cells

raw.rationale: The patient's age, the appearance of the lesion without an identifiable cause, and the histopathological findings of band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone, along with the immunohistochemistry results, are consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma.

rejected.label: angioma
rejected.why: Angioma typically presents as a well-defined, benign vascular lesion, which does not match the ill-defined, atrophic appearance of the lesion in this case.

rejected.label: bacillary angiomatosis
rejected.why: Bacillary angiomatosis is typically associated with systemic symptoms and a distinct histopathological appearance with bacillary forms, which are not mentioned in this case.

rejected.label: pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: Pyogenic granuloma is usually a rapidly growing, bleeding lesion, which does not fit the gradual enlargement and atrophic appearance described.

rejected.label: targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: The absence of hemosiderin deposits, as indicated by the negative Perls Prussian blue stain, does not support this diagnosis.
